title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 1. The Sequence of the Descent
html:
Benediction; the appearance of Vishvambhara; Srivasa bids Murari tell of the Lord; Navadvipa and its devotees; Jagannatha Mishra

Verse 1

स जयत्यतिशुद्धविक्रमः कनकाभः कमलायतेक्षणः।
वरजानुविलम्बिसद्भुजो बहुधा भक्तिरसाभिनर्तकः॥१॥

sa jayatyatiśuddhavikramaḥ kanakābhaḥ kamalāyatekṣaṇaḥ|
varajānuvilambisadbhujo bahudhā bhaktirasābhinartakaḥ||1||

sah — he; jayati — be victorious; ati-shuddha-vikramah — whose prowess is utterly pure; kanaka-abhah — shining like gold; kamala-ayata-ikshanah — with eyes wide as lotuses; vara-janu-vilambi-sad-bhujah — whose fine arms hang down to his beautiful knees; bahudha — in many ways; bhakti-rasa-abhinartakah — dancer in the rasa of devotion.

1Glory to Him! His prowess is utterly pure; He shines like gold; His eyes are wide as lotus petals; His shapely arms reach down to His fine knees; and in many ways He dances in the rasa of devotion.

Verse 2

स जगन्नाथसुतो जगत्पतिर्जगदादिर्जगदार्तिहा विभुः।
कलिपाता कलिभारहारकोऽजनि शच्यां निजभक्तिमुद्वहन्॥२॥

sa jagannāthasuto jagatpatirjagadādirjagadārtihā vibhuḥ|
kalipātā kalibhārahārako'jani śacyāṁ nijabhaktimudvahan||2||

sah — he; jagannatha-sutah — the son of Jagannatha; jagat-patih — the lord of the world; jagat-adih — the origin of the world; jagat-arti-ha — remover of the world's distress; vibhuh — the all-powerful; kali-pata — protector in the Kali age; kali-bhara-harakah — remover of the burden of Kali; ajani — was born; shachyam — of Shachi; nija-bhaktim — devotion to himself; udvahan — bearing.

2He — the son of Jagannatha, Lord and origin of the world, the all-powerful one who takes away the world's distress, protector in the age of Kali and remover of its burden — was born of Shachi, bringing with Him devotion to Himself.

Verse 3

स नवद्वीपवतीषु भूमिषु द्विजवर्यैरभिनन्दितो हरिः।
निजपित्रोः सुखदो गृहे सुखं निवसन् वेदषडङ्गसंहिताम्॥३॥

sa navadvīpavatīṣu bhūmiṣu dvijavaryairabhinandito hariḥ|
nijapitroḥ sukhado gṛhe sukhaṁ nivasan vedaṣaḍaṅgasaṁhitām||3||

sah — he; navadvipa-vatishu — of Navadvipa; bhumishu — in the lands; dvija-varyaih — by the best of the twice-born; abhinanditah — welcomed; harih — Hari; nija-pitroh — to his parents; sukha-dah — giving joy; grihe — at home; sukham — happily; nivasan — living; veda-shad-anga-samhitam — the collection of the Vedas with their six limbs (object of the verb in v. 4).

3Welcomed by the best of the twice-born in the lands of Navadvipa, Hari lived happily at home, a joy to His parents; and the Veda with its six limbs1

Verse 4

निपपाठ गुरोर्गृहे वसन् परिचर्याभिरतः शुचिव्रतः।
स च विश्वम्भरसंज्ञको हरिर्युगधर्माचरणाय धर्मिणाम्॥४॥

nipapāṭha gurorgṛhe vasan paricaryābhirataḥ śucivrataḥ|
sa ca viśvambharasaṁjñako hariryugadharmācaraṇāya dharmiṇām||4||

nipapatha — studied; guroh — of the guru; grihe — in the house; vasan — living; paricharya-abhiratah — devoted to service; shuchi-vratah — pure in his vows; sah — he; cha — and; vishvambhara-samjnakah — called Vishvambhara; harih — Hari; yuga-dharma-acharanaya — for the practice of the dharma of the age; dharminam — of the righteous.

4He studied while living in His guru's house, devoted to serving him and pure in His vows. And this same Hari, called Vishvambhara, so that the righteous might follow the dharma of the age,

Verse 5

हरिकीर्तनमादिशत् स्मरन् पुरुषार्थाय हरेरतिप्रियम्।
स गयासु पितृक्रियां चरन् हरिपादाङ्कितभूमिषु स्वयम्॥५॥

harikīrtanamādiśat smaran puruṣārthāya hareratipriyam|
sa gayāsu pitṛkriyāṁ caran haripādāṅkitabhūmiṣu svayam||5||

hari-kirtanam — the kirtana of Hari; adishat — enjoined; smaran — remembering; purusha-arthaya — for the goal of human life; hareh — to Hari; ati-priyam — very dear; sah — he; gayasu — in Gaya; pitri-kriyam — the rite for the ancestors; charan — performing; hari-pada-ankita-bhumishu — in the lands marked by Hari's feet; svayam — himself.

5enjoined the kirtana of Hari for the sake of man's highest goal, remembering that it is dear beyond measure to Hari. And when He Himself was performing the rite for His ancestors at Gaya, in the land marked by Hari's feet,

Verse 6

निजसंस्मृतिमात्रसम्पदः पुलकप्रेमजडो बभूव ह।
स तदा निजमेव मन्दिरं समगादशरीरया गिरा॥६॥

nijasaṁsmṛtimātrasampadaḥ pulakapremajaḍo babhūva ha|
sa tadā nijameva mandiraṁ samagādaśarīrayā girā||6||

nija-samsmriti-matra-sampadah — from the wealth of the mere remembrance of himself; pulaka-prema-jadah — stunned with love, his hair standing on end; babhuva ha — became; sah — he; tada — then; nijam eva — to his own; mandiram — home; samagat — went back; ashariraya — by a bodiless; gira — voice.

6the mere remembrance of Himself — that treasure — left Him stunned with love, the hair of His body standing on end. Then, at the word of a bodiless voice2, He returned to His own home.

Verse 7

भक्तवर्गमुखवेष्टितः प्रभुः प्रेमपाकपरिपूर्णविग्रहः।
हरिकीर्तनसत्कथासुखं मुमुदे दानवसिंहमर्दनः॥७॥

bhaktavargamukhaveṣṭitaḥ prabhuḥ premapākaparipūrṇavigrahaḥ|
harikīrtanasatkathāsukhaṁ mumude dānavasiṁhamardanaḥ||7||

bhakta-varga-mukha-veshtitah — surrounded by the foremost of the band of devotees; prabhuh — the Lord; prema-paka-paripurna-vigrahah — whose form was full of ripened love; hari-kirtana-sat-katha-sukham — in the joy of the kirtana of Hari and of holy talks; mumude — rejoiced; danava-simha-mardanah — the crusher of the lion-like Danavas.

7Surrounded by the foremost of His devotees, the Lord — the crusher of the lions among the Danavas, whose form was filled with ripened love — gave Himself joyfully to the kirtana of Hari and to holy talk of Him.

Verse 8

अथास्य कीर्तिं श्रवणामृतं सतामुदारकीर्तेः श्रुतिभिः पिपासुभिः।
विगाहितुं श्रीयुतसत्कथां शुभामुवाह हर्षाश्रुविलोललोचनः॥८॥

athāsya kīrtiṁ śravaṇāmṛtaṁ satāmudārakīrteḥ śrutibhiḥ pipāsubhiḥ|
vigāhituṁ śrīyutasatkathāṁ śubhāmuvāha harṣāśruvilolalocanaḥ||8||

atha — then; asya — of him; kirtim — the fame; shravana-amritam — nectar for the ears; satam — of the virtuous; udara-kirteh — of generous fame; shrutibhih — with ears; pipasubhih — thirsting; vigahitum — to plunge into; shri-yuta-sat-katham — the splendid true narrative; shubham — auspicious; uvaha — took up; harsha-ashru-vilola-lochanah — his eyes trembling with tears of joy.

8And then, so that thirsting ears might plunge into the glory of Him whose fame is noble — a glory that is nectar to the ears of the virtuous — one whose eyes were brimming with trembling tears of joy took up this splendid, auspicious and true narrative3.

Verse 9

भक्तः श्रीवासनामा द्विजकुलकमलप्रोल्लसच्चित्रभानुः
प्राहेदं श्रीमुरारिं त्वमिह वद हरेः श्रीचरित्रं नवीनम्।
तस्याज्ञामाकलय्य प्रकटकरपुटैस्तं नमस्कृत्य भूयः
श्रीमच्चैतन्यमूर्तेः कलिकलुषहरां कीर्तिमाह स्वयं सः॥९॥

bhaktaḥ śrīvāsanāmā dvijakulakamalaprollasaccitrabhānuḥ
prāhedaṁ śrīmurāriṁ tvamiha vada hareḥ śrīcaritraṁ navīnam|
tasyājñāmākalayya prakaṭakarapuṭaistaṁ namaskṛtya bhūyaḥ
śrīmaccaitanyamūrteḥ kalikaluṣaharāṁ kīrtimāha svayaṁ saḥ||9||

bhaktah — the devotee; shrivasa-nama — named Srivasa; dvija-kula-kamala-prollasat-chitrabhanuh — the sun that makes the lotus of the twice-born race bloom; praha — said; idam — this; shri-murarim — to Sri Murari; tvam — you; iha — here; vada — tell; hareh — of Hari; shri-charitram — the holy life; navinam — new; tasya — his; ajnam — command; akalayya — accepting; prakata-kara-putaih — with openly joined palms; tam — to him; namaskritya — bowing; bhuyah — again and again; shrimach-chaitanya-murteh — of the embodied Sriman Chaitanya; kali-kalusha-haram — removing the stain of Kali; kirtim — the glory; aha — told; svayam — himself; sah — he.

9A devotee named Srivasa, the sun who makes the lotus of the twice-born race bloom, said to Sri Murari: "Tell here a new and holy account of Hari's life." Accepting his command, Murari openly joined his palms, bowed to him again and again, and himself began to tell the glory of Sriman Chaitanya, which washes away the stain of Kali.

Verse 10

अथ स चिन्तयामास वैद्यसूनुर्मुरारिकः।
कथं वक्ष्यामि बह्वर्थां चैतन्यस्य कथां शुभाम्॥१०॥

atha sa cintayāmāsa vaidyasūnurmurārikaḥ|
kathaṁ vakṣyāmi bahvarthāṁ caitanyasya kathāṁ śubhām||10||

atha — then; sah — he; chintayam asa — reflected; vaidya-sunuh — the physician's son; murarikah — Murari; katham — how; vakshyami — shall I tell; bahu-artham — rich in meaning; chaitanyasya — of Chaitanya; katham — the story; shubham — auspicious.

10Then Murari, the physician's son, reflected: "How shall I tell the auspicious story of Chaitanya, so rich in meaning,

Verse 11

यद्वक्तुं नैव शक्नोति वाचस्पतिरपि स्वयम्।
तथापि वैष्णवादेशं कर्तुं युक्तं मतिर्मम॥११॥

yadvaktuṁ naiva śaknoti vācaspatirapi svayam|
tathāpi vaiṣṇavādeśaṁ kartuṁ yuktaṁ matirmama||11||

yat — which; vaktum — to tell; na eva — not at all; shaknoti — is able; vachaspatih — Vachaspati; api — even; svayam — himself; tatha api — yet; vaishnava-adesham — the command of a Vaishnava; kartum — to carry out; yuktam — is fitting; matih — the thought; mama — my.

11which even Vachaspati4 himself cannot tell? And yet it is right to carry out a Vaishnava's command — so I have resolved;

Verse 12

निर्मला भाति सततं कृष्णस्मरणसम्पदा।
वैष्णवाज्ञा हि फलदा भविष्यति न चान्यथा॥१२॥

nirmalā bhāti satataṁ kṛṣṇasmaraṇasampadā|
vaiṣṇavājñā hi phaladā bhaviṣyati na cānyathā||12||

nirmala — pure (my thought); bhati — shines; satatam — ever; krishna-smarana-sampada — by the wealth of remembering Krishna; vaishnava-ajna — the Vaishnava's command; hi — surely; phala-da — fruitful; bhavishyati — will be; na — not; cha — and; anyatha — otherwise.

12and my resolve shines ever pure through the treasure of remembering Krishna. A Vaishnava's command is sure to bear fruit — it cannot be otherwise."

Verse 13

इत्युक्त्वा वक्तुमारेभे भगवद्भक्तिबृंहिताम्।
कथां धर्मार्थकामाय मोक्षाय विष्णुभक्तये॥१३॥

ityuktvā vaktumārebhe bhagavadbhaktibṛṁhitām|
kathāṁ dharmārthakāmāya mokṣāya viṣṇubhaktaye||13||

iti — thus; uktva — having said; vaktum — to tell; arebhe — began; bhagavad-bhakti-brimhitam — enriched with devotion to Bhagavan; katham — the story; dharma-artha-kamaya — for dharma, wealth and desire; mokshaya — for liberation; vishnu-bhaktaye — for devotion to Vishnu.

13With these words he began to tell the story, steeped in devotion to Bhagavan — for the sake of dharma, wealth and pleasure, for liberation, and for devotion to Vishnu.

Verse 14

नमामि चैतन्यमजं पुरातनं
चतुर्भुजं शङ्खगदाब्जचक्रिणम्।
श्रीवत्सलक्ष्माङ्कितवक्षसं हरिं
सद्भालसंलग्नमणिं सुवाससम्॥१४॥

namāmi caitanyamajaṁ purātanaṁ
caturbhujaṁ śaṅkhagadābjacakriṇam|
śrīvatsalakṣmāṅkitavakṣasaṁ hariṁ
sadbhālasaṁlagnamaṇiṁ suvāsasam||14||

namami — I bow; chaitanyam — to Chaitanya; ajam — the unborn; puratanam — the primeval; chatur-bhujam — four-armed; shankha-gada-abja-chakrinam — bearing conch, mace, lotus and disc; shrivatsa-lakshma-ankita-vakshasam — whose chest is marked with the sign of Shrivatsa; harim — Hari; sad-bhala-samlagna-manim — with a gem set on his fair forehead; su-vasasam — finely clad.

14I bow to Chaitanya — the unborn, the ancient Hari, four-armed, bearing conch, mace, lotus and disc. His chest is marked with the sign of Shrivatsa, a gem rests on His fair brow, and His garments are fine.

Verse 15

वदामि काञ्चिद्भगवत्कथां सतां
हर्षाय किञ्चित्स्खलनं यदा भवेत्।
तदात्र संशोधयितुं महत्तमाः
प्रमाणमेवात्र परोपकारिणः॥१५॥

vadāmi kāñcidbhagavatkathāṁ satāṁ
harṣāya kiñcitskhalanaṁ yadā bhavet|
tadātra saṁśodhayituṁ mahattamāḥ
pramāṇamevātra paropakāriṇaḥ||15||

vadami — I shall tell; kanchit — some; bhagavat-katham — story of Bhagavan; satam — of the virtuous; harshaya — for the delight; kinchit — some; skhalanam — slip; yada — if; bhavet — should occur; tada — then; atra — here; samshodhayitum — to correct; mahattamah — the greatest souls; pramanam — the authority; eva — indeed; atra — in this; para-upakarinah — who do good to others.

15For the delight of the virtuous I shall tell something of the stories of Bhagavan. Should some slip occur, to correct it is the task of the greatest souls, those who do good to others: in this they alone are the measure.

Verse 16

नवद्वीप इति ख्याते क्षेत्रे परमवैष्णवे।
ब्राह्मणाः साधवः शान्ता वैष्णवाः सत्कुलोद्भवाः॥१६॥

navadvīpa iti khyāte kṣetre paramavaiṣṇave|
brāhmaṇāḥ sādhavaḥ śāntā vaiṣṇavāḥ satkulodbhavāḥ||16||

navadvipe — Navadvipa; iti — thus; khyate — known as; kshetre — in the holy place; parama-vaishnave — supremely Vaishnava; brahmanah — brahmanas; sadhavah — saintly; shantah — peaceful; vaishnavah — Vaishnavas; sat-kula-udbhavah — born in good families.

16In the holy land called Navadvipa, devoted wholly to Vishnu, live brahmanas — saintly, peaceful Vaishnavas of good families,

Verse 17

महान्तः कर्मनिपुणाः सर्वे शास्त्रार्थपारगाः।
अन्ये च सन्ति बहुशो भिषक्शूद्रवणिग्जनाः॥१७॥

mahāntaḥ karmanipuṇāḥ sarve śāstrārthapāragāḥ|
anye ca santi bahuśo bhiṣakśūdravaṇigjanāḥ||17||

mahantah — great; karma-nipunah — skilled in rites; sarve — all; shastra-artha-paragah — masters of the meaning of the scriptures; anye — others; cha — and; santi — there are; bahushah — in great numbers; bhishak-shudra-vanig-janah — physicians, shudras and merchants.

17great souls, skilled in rites, every one a master of the meaning of the scriptures; and many other people live there too — physicians, shudras and merchants.

Verse 18

स्वाचारनिरताः शुद्धाः सर्वे विद्योपजीविनः।
तत्र देवव्रताः सर्वे वैकुण्ठभवनोपमे॥१८॥

svācāraniratāḥ śuddhāḥ sarve vidyopajīvinaḥ|
tatra devavratāḥ sarve vaikuṇṭhabhavanopame||18||

sva-achara-niratah — devoted to their own duties; shuddhah — pure; sarve — all; vidya-upajivinah — living by learning; tatra — there; deva-vratah — vowed to God; sarve — all; vaikuntha-bhavana-upame — (in that place) like the abode of Vaikuntha.

18All of them are true to their own duties and pure; all live by learning; all have vowed themselves to God — in that place, which is like the abode of Vaikuntha.

Verse 19

श्रीवासो यत्र रेजे हरिपदकमलप्रोल्लसन्मत्तभृङ्गः
प्रेमार्द्रोद्धूतबाहुः परमरसमदैर्गायतीशं सदोत्कः।
गोपीनाथो द्विजाग्र्यः श्रवणपथगते नाम्नि कृष्णस्य मत्तो-
ऽत्युच्चै रौति स्म भूयो लयतरलकरो नृत्यति स्मातिवेलम्॥१९॥

śrīvāso yatra reje haripadakamalaprollasanmattabhṛṅgaḥ
premārdroddhūtabāhuḥ paramarasamadairgāyatīśaṁ sadotkaḥ|
gopīnātho dvijāgryaḥ śravaṇapathagate nāmni kṛṣṇasya matto-
'tyuccai rauti sma bhūyo layataralakaro nṛtyati smātivelam||19||

shrivasah — Srivasa; yatra — where; reje — shone; hari-pada-kamala-prollasan-matta-bhringah — an intoxicated bee sporting at Hari's lotus feet; prema-ardra-uddhuta-bahuh — moist with love, with arms flung up; parama-rasa-madaih — in the rapture of the highest rasa; gayati — sings; isham — the Lord; sada-utkah — ever eager; gopinathah — Gopinatha; dvija-agryah — foremost of the twice-born; shravana-patha-gate — having reached the path of hearing; namni — the name; krishnasya — of Krishna; mattah — intoxicated; ati-uchchaih — very loudly; rauti sma — cried; bhuyah — again; laya-tarala-karah — his hands quivering in rhythm; nrityati sma — danced; ati-velam — beyond measure.

19There shone Srivasa, an intoxicated bee sporting at Hari's lotus feet: wet with the tears of love, his arms flung up5, ever eager, he sings of the Lord in the rapture of the highest rasa. There too was Gopinatha6, foremost of the twice-born: as soon as the name of Krishna reached his ears, he would weep aloud again and again in his intoxication and dance beyond all measure, his hands quivering to the rhythm.

Verse 20

बालोद्यद्भास्कराभो बुधजनकमलोद्बोधने दक्षमूर्तिः
कारुण्याब्धिहिमांशोरिव जनहृदयोत्तापशान्त्येकमूर्तिः।
प्रेमध्यानातिदक्षो नटनविधिकलासद्गुणाढ्यो महात्मा
श्रीयुक्ताद्वैतवर्यः परमरसकलाचार्य ईशो विरेजे॥२०॥

bālodyadbhāskarābho budhajanakamalodbodhane dakṣamūrtiḥ
kāruṇyābdhihimāṁśoriva janahṛdayottāpaśāntyekamūrtiḥ|
premadhyānātidakṣo naṭanavidhikalāsadguṇāḍhyo mahātmā
śrīyuktādvaitavaryaḥ paramarasakalācārya īśo vireje||20||

bala-udyad-bhaskara-abhah — radiant as the rising morning sun; budha-jana-kamala-udbodhane — in awakening the lotuses that are the wise; daksha-murtih — skilful; karunya-abdhi-himamshoh — of the moon of the ocean of compassion; iva — like; jana-hridaya-uttapa-shanti-eka-murtih — the very embodiment of cooling the burning of people's hearts; prema-dhyana-ati-dakshah — supreme in loving meditation; natana-vidhi-kala-sad-guna-adhyah — rich in the fine gift of the art of dance; maha-atma — the great soul; shri-yukta-advaita-varyah — the excellent Sri Advaita; parama-rasa-kala-acharyah — teacher of the art of the highest rasa; ishah — the master; vireje — shone.

20There shone the lord Sri Advaita, the most excellent, the great soul. Radiant as the rising morning sun, He knew how to awaken the wise as the sun awakens lotuses; like the moon born of the ocean of compassion, He was the one embodiment of the peace that cools the burning in people's hearts. Unsurpassed in loving meditation, rich in the fine gift of the art of dance, He was a teacher of the art of the highest rasa.

Verse 21

यत्र सर्वगुणवानतिरेजे चन्द्रशेखरगुरुर्द्विजराजः।
कृष्णनामकृषिताङ्गरुहः स प्रस्खलन्नयनवारिभिरार्द्रः॥२१॥

yatra sarvaguṇavānatireje candraśekharagururdvijarājaḥ|
kṛṣṇanāmakṛṣitāṅgaruhaḥ sa praskhalannayanavāribhirārdraḥ||21||

yatra — where; sarva-gunavan — endowed with every virtue; ati-reje — shone brightly; chandrashekhara-guruh — the teacher Chandrashekhara; dvija-rajah — king of the twice-born; krishna-nama-krishita-anga-ruhah — the hair of whose body stood on end at the name of Krishna; sah — he; praskhalan-nayana-varibhih — with streaming tears; ardrah — wet.

21There shone brightly the teacher Chandrashekhara, king of the twice-born7, endowed with every virtue: at the name of Krishna the hair of his body stood on end, and he was wet with streaming tears.

Verse 22

यत्र नृत्यति मुनौ हरिदासे दासवत्सलतया जगदीशः।
खेचरैः सुरगणैः समहेशैर्लास्यमाशु परिपश्यति हृष्टः॥२२॥

yatra nṛtyati munau haridāse dāsavatsalatayā jagadīśaḥ|
khecaraiḥ suragaṇaiḥ samaheśairlāsyamāśu paripaśyati hṛṣṭaḥ||22||

yatra — where; nrityati — while dancing; munau — the sage; haridase — Haridasa; dasa-vatsalataya — out of love for his servant; jagat-ishah — the Lord of the world; khecharaih — moving in the sky; sura-ganaih — with the hosts of gods; sa-maheshaih — together with Mahesha; lasyam — the dance; ashu — at once; paripashyati — watches; hrishtah — delighted.

22There, when the sage Haridasa dances, the Lord of the world, out of love for His servant, at once looks on that dance with delight, together with the hosts of gods who roam the sky, and with Mahesha.

Verse 23

यत्र विष्णुपदसम्भवा सरिद्वेगवत्यतितरां करुणार्द्रा।
स्पर्धया रविसुतासरयूणां या दधार कनकोज्ज्वलं हरिम्॥२३॥

yatra viṣṇupadasambhavā saridvegavatyatitarāṁ karuṇārdrā|
spardhayā ravisutāsarayūṇāṁ yā dadhāra kanakojjvalaṁ harim||23||

yatra — where; vishnu-pada-sambhava — born from Vishnu's foot; sarit — the river; vegavati — swift; ati-taram — exceedingly; karuna-ardra — moist with compassion; spardhaya — in rivalry; ravi-suta-sarayunam — with the daughter of the Sun (the Yamuna) and the Sarayu; ya — who; dadhara — bore; kanaka-ujjvalam — shining like gold; harim — Hari.

23There flows the river born from Vishnu's foot — swift, and brimming with the waters of compassion; vying with the Yamuna, daughter of the Sun, and with the Sarayu, she has received Hari, shining like gold8.

Verse 24

जगन्नाथस्तस्मिन् द्विजकुलपयोधीन्दुसदृशो-
ऽभवद्वेदाचार्यः सकलगुणयुक्तो गुरुसमः।
स कृष्णाङ्घ्रिध्यानप्रबलतरयोगेन मनसा
विशुद्धः प्रेमार्द्रो नवशशिकलेवाशु ववृधे॥२४॥

jagannāthastasmin dvijakulapayodhīndusadṛśo-
'bhavadvedācāryaḥ sakalaguṇayukto gurusamaḥ|
sa kṛṣṇāṅghridhyānaprabalatarayogena manasā
viśuddhaḥ premārdro navaśaśikalevāśu vavṛdhe||24||

jagannathah — Jagannatha; tasmin — in it (Navadvipa); dvija-kula-payodhi-indu-sadrishah — like the moon in the ocean of the twice-born race; abhavat — there was; veda-acharyah — a teacher of the Vedas; sakala-guna-yuktah — endowed with all virtues; guru-samah — equal to Guru (Brihaspati); sah — he; krishna-anghri-dhyana-prabala-tara-yogena — by the mighty yoga of meditation on Krishna's feet; manasa — in mind; vishuddhah — purified; prema-ardrah — moist with love; nava-shashi-kala — the crescent of the new moon; iva — like; ashu — swiftly; vavridhe — grew.

24There lived Jagannatha — like the moon risen from the ocean of the twice-born race — a teacher of the Vedas, endowed with all virtues, equal to Brihaspati. His mind purified by the mighty yoga of meditation on Krishna's feet, his heart melting with love, he swiftly waxed like the crescent of the new moon.

Thus ends the first sarga, "The Sequence of the Descent" (Avatara-anukrama), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Chaitanya-charita."

✦

Notes

  1. The six angas (auxiliary disciplines) of the Veda: phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, metrics and astronomy.
  2. The "bodiless voice" (asharira vak) is a voice from the sky, heard without a visible speaker.
  3. The subject is not named; to judge from the next verse, it is the poet himself, Murari Gupta.
  4. Vachaspati ("lord of speech") is Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods, the model of eloquence.
  5. The beginning of the second line of this verse is damaged in the sources; "his arms flung up" is a tentative reading restored by the metre.
  6. Gopinatha is a brahmana of Navadvipa; apparently Gopinatha Acharya, who later appears in Nilachala.
  7. "King of the twice-born" (dvija-raja) is also a poetic name of the moon — a play on the name Chandrashekhara ("Crowned with the Moon").
  8. On the banks of the Yamuna Krishna played, on the banks of the Sarayu (in Ayodhya) Rama; the Ganga at Navadvipa has received Gaura.
